decision.summary: Tenant wants to replace the landlord's broken LG washing machine with their own. This is a consent request, not yet a repair. I asked the landlord for consent and for who pays removal and fitting and what happens to their machine. I updated the tenant and put the ticket on hold with a review on 29 July.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: At intake, routine. Outstanding: landlord consent to the tenant's own replacement, who pays removal and fitting, and what happens to the landlord's machine. The fault is undiagnosed.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Landlord consent request (APR-101) to the landlord via the agency landlord record, and an email update to the tenant. Ticket on hold, review 2025-07-29.

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: No human escalation. The decision belongs to the landlord, which is already requested. A human is needed only if the landlord stays silent after the chase.

args.decision_needed: Tenant reports the LG washing machine provided with the flat has a power failure and says it cannot be fixed (their own web research, not a diagnosis). They offer to buy a replacement at their own cost, which would remain their property and be removed when they leave. Do you consent? If so, who pays to disconnect and remove the existing machine and fit the new one, and what should happen to your machine (inspect/repair, dispose)? Alternatively we can send our contractor to inspect and quote.
options: Consent to tenant's own replacement (tenant's item, not on inventory); tell us who pays for removal/fitting and what to do with your machine
Send our contractor to inspect and quote repair/replacement first

args.body: Thanks for letting us know about the washing machine. Because the machine belongs to the landlord, replacing it with your own needs their consent, so we've put your offer to them, including that the new one would stay yours and go with you when you leave. We've also asked who covers removing the old machine and fitting the new one. Please don't remove the current one yet. If you can, send a photo of the machine and any error code. We'll update you by 29 July.
